newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon ceasefire deal monitors adjourn meeting.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon ceasefire deal monitors adjourn meeting.

text.p: A five-nation committee monitoring a ceasefire understanding in Lebanon discussed in a tense session on Sunday Israeli and Lebanese complaints following Israel-Hizbollah fighting, Lebanese officials said.

They said the U.S., French, Syrian, Lebanese and Israeli delegates adjourned the meeting to Tuesday after a four-hour session in the coastal town of Naqoura to weigh a complaint by Beirut that Israel shelled civilian areas in south Lebanon on Thursday.
Israel said it would complain that Hizbollah guerrillas fired on its forces from three villages in the area that day.

It was the fourth meeting of the committee set up to deal with violations of a U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz in April against Hizbollah after exchanges of fire that targeted civilian areas on both sides.
"There was a tense atmosphere in the meeting," one official told Reuters in Beirut, adding the meeting was adjourned because of the Jewish holy day of Yom Kippur, which began at sunset.

"The Lebanese side argued that Israel breached the accord by shelling villages in south Lebanon inhabited by civilians not guerrillas. It said Israel is lodging complaints but it is the one breaching the accord," the source added.

The understanding bars the targeting or launching of attacks from civilian areas by Israeli forces or the pro-Iranian fighters. But it does not bar raids on Israeli forces occupying south Lebanon and gives both sides a self-defence right.
Some 200 Lebanese, mostly civilians, were killed in the April blitz, dubbed by Israel "Operation Grapes of Wrath".

Witnesses have said that during Thursday's clashes between Hizbollah guerrillas and Israeli forces some 50 shells slammed into two villages in the Hizbollah-held Iqlim al-Toufah ridge. A civilian woman was hurt by flying debris caused by a shell.
Two Israeli soldiers were killed and eight wounded in Thursday's fighting. Two Hizbollah guerrillas were also killed.

Hizbollah (Party of God) fighters, who have killed 20 Israeli soldiers this year in south Lebanon, are battling to oust the Israeli forces from the 15-km (nine-mile) deep zone stretching from Mount Lebanon to the Mediterranean.

After an introductory August 8 meeting, the monitoring committee met on August 15 to look into an Israeli complaint about what it said was the killing of a Lebanese civilian by a Hizbollah bomb, a complaint Beirut dismissed as invalid.
It met on September 1 to discuss another Israeli complaint against guerrilla firing in which Israel said two Lebanese residents of the zone were wounded.
Before Sunday's meeting, Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said Saturday's Israeli strikes in south Lebanon were "necessary operations" in retaliation for Hizbollah attacks.

"We are trying in every possible way to lower the tension in the region. We have no intention of taking extraordinary measures, but we have the obligation to take every necessary operation for the good of our forces working in Lebanon," Mordechai told Israel's Channel One television.
